title: The scribe's tables: positional word lists, page memory and a glyph chain
method: One procedure, fitted on the public practice pages only. A scribe writes a book page by page. At each word: (1) with small probability he copies the word just written or a word from the line above, varying its ending by one glyph; 6 times in 10 the variant is a shape his tables do not hold at all. When copying from the line above he prefers a source word that does not also sit four lines back. (2) Otherwise he reaches for tables of how words sit: a successor table keyed on the last glyph of the previous word, a line-opening table, and a line-ending table keyed on the last glyph of the previous line's last word; paragraph-opening first lines follow their own tables. Words he already wrote on this page are 2.5 times likelier to be written again, words from the last 15 pages somewhat likelier. (3) When no table covers the place, 9 times in 100 he writes a word of his own devising, drawn from a fitted glyph chain; otherwise the chain itself is the fallback. Tables are counts from the public pages only; no rule names a target pattern.
